input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: style() tests fg and bg for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so the 256-color index 0 is skipped
- failure path: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0, meaning black, applies no color at all and the text renders in the terminal default; the caller sees no error

Reviewer finding
- description: The check changed from `fg is not None` to truthiness `if fg:`. A color value of 0 (integer 256-color index for black) is falsy, so it is silently skipped.
- rationale: Trigger: `style(text, fg=0)` or `bg=0`. The color is dropped and no escape code is emitted, so the user gets uncolored text instead of black. Previously 0 was valid and emitted `38;5;0`.
critique: The finding identifies the same mechanism: a truthiness check on fg/bg instead of `is not None`, so index 0 is skipped and no color is emitted. It also gives the same trigger, `fg=0`/`bg=0`, and the same silent loss of black.
